source.archive: Cui, Li, and Zhou OSF replication archive
source.source_article: Choshen-Hillel, Shaw, and Caruso (2020), Lying to appear honest
authorized_normalizations: Removed the archive's generic LLM wrapper and all reason-generation requests.
Separated the shared coin-flip/bonus setting from whether true outcomes were revealed.
Removed the contradictory phrase 'when this was revealed' from honesty items in the truth-not-revealed arm and supplied condition-consistent item wording.
Locked the Jim-versus-Dan honesty difference-in-differences as primary; retained goodness ratings, Mark ratings, and the bonus-rule check as secondary.

population.simulation_target: U.S. adult observer rating coin-flip reporters

materials.participant_role: Act as one U.S. adult observer evaluating Jim, Dan, and Mark in the study below. Respond for yourself, do not predict the average person, and do not analyze the experiment.
materials.common_scenario: In a lab experiment, 500 participants privately flipped a coin eight times and reported their number of heads. They received a flat fee plus $0.25 for every reported head.

truth_revealed.label: True outcomes revealed
truth_revealed.stimulus: Jim truly flipped eight heads and reported eight. Dan truly flipped eight heads but reported seven. Mark truly flipped four heads and reported four.

truth_not_revealed.label: True outcomes not revealed
truth_not_revealed.stimulus: Jim reported eight heads. Dan reported seven heads. Mark reported four heads. Their true outcomes are not disclosed.

materials.response_instruction: Rate goodness and honesty from 1 (not at all) to 7 (extremely); answer the bonus-rule check with 1 for yes and 2 for no. Return only integer item responses in the required JSON structure.

text_by_arm.truth_revealed: How honest was Jim, given that he reported eight heads and his revealed true outcome was eight heads?
text_by_arm.truth_not_revealed: Based only on his report of eight heads, how honest does Jim appear?

text_by_arm.truth_revealed: How honest was Dan, given that he reported seven heads and his revealed true outcome was eight heads?
text_by_arm.truth_not_revealed: Based only on his report of seven heads, how honest does Dan appear?

text_by_arm.truth_revealed: How honest was Mark, given that he reported four heads and his revealed true outcome was four heads?
text_by_arm.truth_not_revealed: Based only on his report of four heads, how honest does Mark appear?

items.text: How much do you think Jim is a good person?
How much do you think Dan is a good person?
How much do you think Mark is a good person?
Did participants who reported more heads receive a larger bonus? Use 1 for yes and 2 for no.

research_restricted.aligned_hypothesis_text: Revealing true outcomes increases the honesty advantage of truthful extreme reporting over underreporting, relative to the truth-not-revealed condition.
research_restricted.reversed_hypothesis_text: Revealing true outcomes decreases the honesty advantage of truthful extreme reporting over underreporting, relative to the truth-not-revealed condition.
